sentences.zh: 战争。

sentences.en: And Hamilcar himself is a very seasoned Roman fighter.
sentences.zh: 哈米尔卡本人是一位经验丰富的罗马战将。

sentences.en: So it's Hamilcar, in the dying days of the
sentences.zh: 所以在

sentences.en: First Punic War, who had led the desperate attempt by the Carthaginians in Sicily to defeat the Romans there.
sentences.zh: 第一次布匿战争行将结束时，正是哈米尔卡率领迦太基人在西西里进行了绝望的尝试，试图在那里击败罗马人。

sentences.en: It fails basically because the Carthaginian fleet is defeated and so therefore Hamilcar can no longer be supplied from Carthage.
sentences.zh: 之所以失败，主要是因为迦太基舰队战败了，因此哈米尔卡无法再从迦太基获得补给。

sentences.en: And when Carthage is thereby forced to surrender in the war, it's
sentences.zh: 当迦太基因此被迫在这场战争中投降时，

sentences.en: Hamilcar who is entrusted by the Carthaginians to negotiate the terMs. And people who listened to our
sentences.zh: 正是哈米尔卡被迦太基人委以重任去谈判条款。听过我们

sentences.en: episode about this may remember that in the wake of Carthage's defeat, they're so skint that they can't afford to pay the mercenaries who provided them with the bulk of their army.
sentences.zh: 关于这一集的听众可能还记得，在迦太基战败之后，他们穷得叮当响，根本付不起为他们提供主力军队的雇佣兵的薪水。

sentences.en: The mercenaries rebel.
sentences.zh: 雇佣兵叛变了。

sentences.en: At one point, it looks as though Carthage is going to fall to them.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，迦太基看起来似乎要落入他们手中。

sentences.en: And it's Hamilcar, who returns from Sicily, leads the campaign against the mercenaries and ends up defeating them and executing them all in very horrible and bloody ways.
sentences.zh: 正是从西西里返回的哈米尔卡，领导了针对雇佣兵的战役，并最终击败了他们，用各种极其恐怖和血腥的方式将他们全部处决。

sentences.en: That was a satisfyingly bloody story, wasn't it?
sentences.zh: 那是一个令人大快朵颐的血腥故事，不是吗？

sentences.en: The defeat of the mercenaries.
sentences.zh: 击败雇佣兵。

sentences.en: So, I mean, he hates Rome.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，他痛恨罗马。

sentences.en: He has massive, massive unfinished business with Rome, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 他和罗马之间有大量、大量的血海深仇未了，对吧？

sentences.en: But it's more than just political.
sentences.zh: 但这不仅仅是政治上的。

sentences.en: It's personal for Hamilcar.
sentences.zh: 对哈米尔卡来说，这是私仇。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: He resents Rome as an opponent in war who has defeated Carthage.
sentences.zh: 他痛恨罗马这个在战争中击败了迦太基的对手。

sentences.en: So that's understandable.
sentences.zh: 所以这情有可原。

sentences.en: But in due course, his resentment of that, I think, is definitely spiced by a personal sense of betrayal.
sentences.zh: 但久而久之，我认为他对这种事的怨恨，绝对夹杂了一种被背叛的个人感受。

sentences.en: Because Hamilcar has negotiated these terms with the Romans.
sentences.zh: 因为哈米尔卡是和罗马人谈判这些条款的人。

sentences.en: And the Romans take advantage of the mercenary war to tighten the screws on Carthage.
sentences.zh: 罗马人利用雇佣兵战争的机会，进一步对迦太基施压。

sentences.en: So essentially exploiting her misfortune.
sentences.zh: 也就是趁火打劫。

sentences.en: So in 237, that is the year after the defeat of the mercenaries, the Carthaginians
sentences.zh: 因此在公元前237年，也就是击败雇佣兵的第二年，迦太基人

sentences.en: want to go and stabilize their position in Sardinia because there have been kind of mercenary uprisings there as well.
sentences.zh: 想要前往并稳固他们在萨丁尼亚的地位，因为那里也爆发了某种雇佣兵起义。

sentences.en: So they raise an army to go and do that.
sentences.zh: 于是他们集结了一支军队前去处理此事。

sentences.en: And the Romans, in a display of coarse and brutal cynicism that is entirely typical of their statecraft, denounce this army as being in breach of the treaty.
sentences.zh: 而罗马人则表现出一种粗暴且冷酷的玩世不恭，这完全符合他们一贯的治国风格，他们谴责这支军队违反了条约。

sentences.en: They say, you're raising this army to come and attack us.
sentences.zh: 他们说，你们集结这支军队是来攻击我们的。

sentences.en: And so a Roman embassy arrives in Carthage to demand revisions to the peace treaty because they say that the
sentences.zh: 因此，一个罗马使团抵达迦太基，要求修改和平条约，因为他们声称

sentences.en: Carthaginians have broken it.
sentences.zh: 迦太基人撕毁了条约。

sentences.en: They haven't broken it at all.
sentences.zh: 他们根本没有撕毁条约。

sentences.en: And the Romans say, you've got to surrender Sardinia and Corsica to us.
sentences.zh: 罗马人却说，你们必须把萨丁尼亚和科西嘉割让给我们。

sentences.en: This was never part of the original treaty.
sentences.zh: 这在最初的条约里根本没有提及。

sentences.en: And we are going to increase the indemnity that you need to pay us.
sentences.zh: 而且我们还要提高你们需要支付给我们的赔款。

sentences.en: So essentially, it is massively exploiting
sentences.zh: 所以本质上，这极大地利用了

sentences.en: Carthage's hour of need and weakness.
sentences.zh: 迦太基人最需要帮助和最虚弱的时刻。

sentences.en: And so they have no choice but to accept these terMs.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们别无选择，只能接受这些条款。

sentences.en: And Hamilcar is left incredibly embittered.
sentences.zh: 哈米尔卡感到无比愤怒与痛心。

sentences.en: So to quote a historian of the period, resentful of the injustice, but powerless to prevent it.
sentences.zh: 用当时一位历史学家的话说，对这种不公充满怨恨，却又无力阻止。

sentences.en: So this is not a kind of man who is going to take it lying down.
sentences.zh: 所以他可不是那种会逆来顺受的人。

sentences.en: So how can he go about doing this, Tom?
sentences.zh: 那么他该如何着手呢，汤姆？

sentences.en: Because you said earlier that Carthage has been hamstrung.
sentences.zh: 因为你之前说过迦太基已经被束缚了手脚。

sentences.en: So how can they plausibly hope to go toe-to-toe with the Romans once again?
sentences.zh: 既然如此，他们怎么还能奢望再次与罗马人一决高下呢？

sentences.en: Well, so they've lost their land empire in Sicily, in Sardinia and Corsica.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们失去了在西红柿、萨丁尼亚和科西嘉的陆地帝国。

sentences.en: But there is another obvious place where Hamilcar can start building a power center.
sentences.zh: 但还有一个显而易见的地方，哈米尔卡可以在那里建立权力中心。

sentences.en: And this is Spain.
sentences.zh: 这就是西班牙。

sentences.en: So I mentioned that
sentences.zh: 所以我刚才提到

sentences.en: Phoenician colonies have been planted along the southern coast of Spain and actually beyond the pillars of Hercules, so the Straits of Gibraltar.
sentences.zh: 腓尼基殖民地已经遍布西班牙南部海岸，甚至延伸到了大力神之柱以外，也就是直布罗陀海峡。

sentences.en: Probably the oldest of the lot is Gardez, which will become Cadiz.
sentences.zh: 其中历史最悠久的可能就是加德斯了，后来变成了加的斯。

sentences.en: And these settlements are very strategically positioned.
sentences.zh: 这些定居点具有极具战略意义的地理位置。

sentences.en: So as with Carthage, very rich agricultural hinterland.
sentences.zh: 和迦太基一样，这里有着非常富饶的农业腹地。

sentences.en: So there's opportunity there to expand.
sentences.zh: 因此这里有扩张的机会。

sentences.en: But even more, it is potentially incredibly rich because there are a lot of precious minerals just waiting to be mined.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，这里还蕴藏着巨大的潜在财富，因为有大量珍贵矿产正等待开采。

sentences.en: And also, if these minerals can be kind of turned into gold to pay for mercenaries to conquer more
sentences.zh: 而且，如果这些矿产能够变成黄金，用来支付雇佣兵去征服更多

sentences.en: territory, then that conquered territory can supply further troops because Spain is obviously a massive, massive reserve of manpower.
sentences.zh: 领土，那么被征服的领土就能提供更多的军队，因为西班牙显然是一个庞大无比的人力资源库。

sentences.en: Carthage has never actually established a land empire in Spain.
sentences.zh: 迦太基实际上从未在西班牙建立过陆地帝国。

sentences.en: To repeat, it is not a city that is interested in establishing kind of direct rule over vast swathes in the way that the Romans have shown themselves to be.
sentences.zh: 重申一遍，它不是一个热衷于像罗马人那样对广袤土地进行直接统治的城市。

sentences.en: But Hamilcar, having looked at the way that Rome has risen to power, recognizes, I think, that the only way that Carthage can really survive, let alone
sentences.zh: 但哈米尔卡在观察了罗马的崛起方式后，我认为他意识到，迦太基要想真正生存下去，更不用说

sentences.en: defeat the Romans, is to play that game as well.
sentences.zh: 击败罗马人，唯一的办法就是也玩这个游戏。

sentences.en: And so his plan essentially is to transform the kind of loose hegemony that Carthage had always exercised over these Phoenician colonies in Spain into a kind of direct rule.
sentences.zh: 所以他的基本计划是，将迦太基过去对西班牙这些腓尼基殖民地一直行使的某种松散霸权，转变为直接统治。

sentences.en: And then using these Phoenician ports as bases to expand inland and carve out a Spanish
sentences.zh: 然后以这些腓尼基港口为基地向内陆扩张，开辟出一个西班牙

sentences.en: dominion that will be able to replace the empire lost in Sicily, Sardinia and Corsica, and hopefully
sentences.zh: 领地，以此来替代在西西里、萨丁尼亚和科西嘉失去的帝国，并希望

sentences.en: to provide even greater reserves because of the mineral wealth and the possible reserves of manpower.
sentences.zh: 凭借矿产财富和潜在的人力资源，提供更强大的后备力量。

sentences.en: So on paper, this looks like a brilliant plan, right?
sentences.zh: 所以从纸面上看，这真是一个绝妙的计划，对吧？

sentences.en: You can get the silver and the minerals from Spain.
sentences.zh: 你可以从西班牙获取白银和矿产。

sentences.en: You can pick up mercenaries and conscripts from the Iberian peoples.
sentences.zh: 你可以从伊比利亚人中招募雇佣兵和应征入伍者。

sentences.en: You'll be militarily stronger.
sentences.zh: 你的军事实力会更强。

sentences.en: You'll be financially stronger.
sentences.zh: 你的财政实力会更强。

sentences.en: And you can basically begin to rebuild your reputation and you can plausibly hope to have another go at the Romans later on.
sentences.zh: 你基本上可以开始重建声誉，并且可以合理地期望以后再和罗马人较量一番。

sentences.en: And it's also good for
sentences.zh: 而且这对

sentences.en: Hamilcar personally, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 哈米尔卡个人也很有好处，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because if he's able to pull this off, it will entrench his position as the big man in the state.
sentences.zh: 因为如果他能成功做到这一点，将巩固他作为国家大佬的地位。

sentences.en: Does he want to create a dynasty?
sentences.zh: 他想建立一个王朝吗？

sentences.en: I think almost certainly.
sentences.zh: 我想几乎是肯定的。

sentences.en: Politics in Carthage is pretty carnivorous.
sentences.zh: 迦太基的政治非常残酷。

sentences.en: The penalty for failure is very serious.
sentences.zh: 失败的代价极其惨重。

sentences.en: Generals who lose battles are often crucified.
sentences.zh: 战败的将领经常被钉死在十字架上。

sentences.en: So I think for Hamilcar, who has had personal experience of people trying to stab him in the back while he's been busy fighting the Romans,
sentences.zh: 所以对于哈米尔卡来说，他曾亲身经历过在自己忙于对抗罗马人时被人从背后捅刀子的事情，

sentences.en: I think the chance of establishing a great center of power, not just for Carthage, but for himself and establishing a dynasty there, you know, win-win.
sentences.zh: 我认为，建立一个强大的权力中心的机会，不仅是为了迦太基，也是为了他自己，并在那里建立一个王朝，你知道的，双赢。

sentences.en: Everything is great about it.
sentences.zh: 一切都好极了。

sentences.en: And it's very clear that Hamilcar is an extremely enthusiastic family man.
sentences.zh: 而且很明显，哈米尔卡是一个极其顾家的好男人。

sentences.en: So we know he has at least three daughters.
sentences.zh: 我们知道他至少有三个女儿。

sentences.en: We don't know their names, but we do know that one of them is married off to Hamilcar's closest political ally in Carthage, who is a guy called Hasdrubal the Handsome.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道她们的名字，但我们确实知道其中一个嫁给了哈米尔卡在迦太基最亲密的政治盟友，一个叫美男子哈斯德鲁巴的家伙。

sentences.en: And people who remember our first series may also remember the fact that basically they're only about three names in Carthage, of which Hasdrubal is probably the most common.
sentences.zh: 看过我们第一季的观众可能也会记得，基本上迦太基总共只有大约三个名字，其中哈斯德鲁巴可能是最常见的。

sentences.en: So this is Hasdrubal the Handsome, because he's such a good looking guy.
sentences.zh: 这就是美男子哈斯德鲁巴，因为他长得太帅了。

sentences.en: So good news for Hamilcar's daughter.
sentences.zh: 所以这对哈米尔卡的女儿来说是个好消息。

sentences.en: And in 237, when Hamilcar leaves Carthage for Spain, Hasdrubal is sailing with him.
sentences.zh: 公元前237年，当哈米尔卡离开迦太基前往西班牙时，哈斯德鲁巴也随船同行。

sentences.en: Hamilcar also has three sons.
sentences.zh: 哈米尔卡还有三个儿子。

sentences.en: The youngest of these is called Mago.
sentences.zh: 其中最小的叫马戈。

sentences.en: Then inevitably there's a guy called Hasdrubal.
sentences.zh: 然后不可避免地，还有一个叫哈斯德鲁巴的家伙。

sentences.en: So that's Hamilcar's son.
sentences.zh: 所以那是哈米尔卡的儿子。

sentences.en: And the oldest is a young lad called Hannibal.
sentences.zh: 最年长的是一个名叫汉尼拔的年轻小伙子。

sentences.en: And this is the Hannibal.
sentences.zh: 这就是那个汉尼拔。

sentences.en: So in 237, when Hamilcar is preparing to leave for Spain, Hannibal is only nine years old.
sentences.zh: 所以在公元前237年，当哈米尔卡准备前往西班牙时，汉尼拔只有九岁。

sentences.en: And you might think that's probably too young to be taken to a war zone.
sentences.zh: 你可能会觉得，被带去战区实在太年轻了。

sentences.en: But Hamilcar thinks not.
sentences.zh: 但哈米尔卡不这么认为。

sentences.en: And there is a very, very famous anecdote with which we finished our last series on Carthage.
sentences.zh: 有一个非常非常著名的轶事，我们用它作为上一季关于迦太基的结尾。

sentences.en: But I think it bears repeating because it is very, very revealing about what will motivate Hannibal.
sentences.zh: 但我认为它值得重温，因为它非常深刻地揭示了汉尼拔的动机之源。

sentences.en: And he tells it to various people later in life.
sentences.zh: 他在晚年时曾向不同的人讲述过这件事。

sentences.en: So it almost certainly comes from his own lips.
sentences.zh: 所以这几乎肯定出自他自己的口述。

sentences.en: And he describes how he joins his father in the great temple of Baal in Carthage, where his father is making sacrifice.
sentences.zh: 他描述了自己如何跟随父亲来到迦太基伟大的巴力神庙，他的父亲在那里进行献祭。

sentences.en: And this is supposedly how Hannibal described it.
sentences.zh: 据称汉尼拔是这样描述的。

sentences.en: The omens proved favorable.
sentences.zh: 占卜结果显示吉利。

sentences.en: Hamilcar poured a libation to the gods and performed the customary ceremonies, after which he ordered all those who were present at the sacrifice
sentences.zh: 哈米尔卡向众神奠酒并举行了惯常的仪式，随后他命令所有参加献祭的人

sentences.en: to stand back a little way from the altar.
sentences.zh: 离祭坛远一点。

sentences.en: Then he called Hannibal to him and asked him affectionately whether he wished to accompany the expedition.
sentences.zh: 接着他把汉尼拔叫到身边，亲切地问他是否想一起去远征。

sentences.en: So that's to Spain.
sentences.zh: 也就是去西班牙。

sentences.en: Hannibal was overjoyed to accept and like a boy begged to be allowed to go.
sentences.zh: 汉尼拔欣喜若狂地接受了，像个小男孩一样恳求允许他同行。

sentences.en: His father then took him by the hand, led him up to the altar and commanded him to lay his hand upon the victim and swear an oath that he would never become a friend to the Romans.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲随后拉起他的手，带他走到祭坛前，命令他将手按在祭品上，并庄严起誓，发誓绝不与罗马人交好。

sentences.en: Strong stuff.
sentences.zh: 够有魄力的。

sentences.en: Strong stuff.
sentences.zh: 够有魄力的。

sentences.en: And it's a promise that he will keep all his life.
sentences.zh: 这是一个他将用一生去践行的承诺。

sentences.en: And you think the Senate day is probably true because Hannibal tells it himself.
sentences.zh: 你觉得这个故事很可能是真的，因为是汉尼拔自己讲的。

sentences.en: He probably is.
sentences.zh: 它很可能就是真的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So first of all, he has to go to Spain and actually this is an unbelievable thing.
sentences.zh: 首先，他必须去西班牙，实际上这是一件令人难以置信的事情。

sentences.en: He goes to
sentences.zh: 他

sentences.en: Spain at the age of nine and he will not return to Carthage until he's 42.
sentences.zh: 九岁时就去了西班牙，直到四十二岁才返回迦太基。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He is raised in this colonial environment, this process of conquest, then of rule in Spain.
sentences.zh: 他在这种殖民环境中长大，经历了征服，然后在西班牙进行统治。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And in due course, he will come to take command of it.
sentences.zh: 不负众望，他最终将接管这一切。

sentences.en: But first, of course, he has to serve his apprenticeship.
sentences.zh: 但首先，他当然必须经历实习期。

sentences.en: And he does this under two formidable men in succession.
sentences.zh: 他在两位 formidable（了不起的）人物手下先后完成了历练。

sentences.en: And the first, of course, is his father, Hamilcar Barker.
sentences.zh: 第一个人当然是他的父亲，哈米尔卡·巴卡。

sentences.en: And even though Hamilcar is probably the most formidable man in
sentences.zh: 尽管哈米尔卡可能是迦太基

sentences.en: Carthage, there's no guarantee of success.
sentences.zh: 最令人畏惧的人，但这并不能保证成功。

sentences.en: He doesn't have that many men.
sentences.zh: 他没有那么多部下。

sentences.en: This is Carthage's whole problem that they don't have a huge citizen body.
sentences.zh: 这就是迦太基的全部问题所在，他们没有庞大的公民群体。

sentences.en: So generally they rely on mercenaries, but now they don't have much money.
sentences.zh: 所以他们通常依赖雇佣兵，但现在他们没有多少钱。

sentences.en: So they can't afford many mercenaries.
sentences.zh: 所以他们雇不起很多雇佣兵。

sentences.en: So the estimation of
sentences.zh: 因此，据德克斯特·霍约斯在他的关于汉尼拔王朝的优秀著作中的估计

sentences.en: Dexter Hoyos in his very good book on this Hannibal's dynasty, he reckons probably Hamilcar is sailing to Spain with about 20,000 men.
sentences.zh: 他估计哈米尔卡带往西班牙的军队大概只有两万人左右。

sentences.en: So not that many at all.
sentences.zh: 所以一点也不多。

sentences.en: And it's not surprising, that being so, he needs money.
sentences.zh: 既然如此，他需要钱也就不足为奇了。

sentences.en: He sails to Gardez, to Gadiz.
sentences.zh: 他扬帆驶向加德斯。

sentences.en: And what he wants is the silver and copper mines along the Rio Tinto that lie about 60 miles inland from Gardez.
sentences.zh: 他想要的是里奥廷托河沿岸的银矿和铜矿，这些矿藏距离加德斯内陆大约60英里。

sentences.en: And which is fake, you know, it's rich across the whole of the Mediterranean.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这在整个地中海都享有盛名，富饶无比。

sentences.en: So it features in the Bible as Tarshish, you know, a land of fabled wealth.
sentences.zh: 所以它在《圣经》中被称为他施，你知道的，一个传说中充满财富的土地。

sentences.en: According to tradition, the tribes who live there are so rich that their cattle troughs are made of silver.
sentences.zh: 根据传统，那里的部落极其富有，连牛槽都是用白银做的。

sentences.en: So obviously if you're a colonial administrator in desperate need of cash, this is exactly the kind of place that you would go straight for.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，如果你是一个极度渴望现金的殖民地行政官，这正是你会直奔而去的地方。

sentences.en: And he does meet with opposition.
sentences.zh: 他也确实遇到了抵抗。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Good news for him though, is that although they're rich, they're not as good at fighting as he is, right?
sentences.zh: 不过对他的好消息是，尽管他们很富有，但他们打仗不如他厉害，对吧？

sentences.en: He will sort of encircle them, won't he?
sentences.zh: 他会包围他们，不是吗？

sentences.en: That's his strategy.
sentences.zh: 这就是他的战略。

sentences.en: He encircles them and then he completely massacres them.
sentences.zh: 他包围他们，然后将他们彻底屠杀。

sentences.en: I mean, he's a pretty ferocious man, Hamilcar Barker.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，哈米尔卡·巴卡是个相当凶猛的人。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: This strategy of surrounding your enemies and then massacring them.
sentences.zh: 这种包围敌人然后屠杀他们的战略。

sentences.en: And if young Hannibal is at his side when he's pursuing these tactics, I mean, this is something that clearly Hannibal will bear in
sentences.zh: 如果年轻的汉尼拔在他实施这些战术时就在他身旁，我的意思是，这显然是汉尼拔日后会牢记在心的东西

sentences.en: mind in due course because it becomes a favourite tactic of Hannibal himself.
sentences.zh: 因为这后来成了汉尼拔本人最喜欢的战术。

sentences.en: And Hamilcar is very brutal in the process of conquering and pacifying Spain.
sentences.zh: 在征服和安抚西班牙的过程中，哈米尔卡手段极其残酷。

sentences.en: So the leaders of tribes who oppose him are tortured and crucified.
sentences.zh: 因此，反抗他的部落领袖会受到酷刑折磨并被钉死在十字架上。

sentences.en: And the Carthaginians are very good at torture as anyone who's listened to our episode on the war with the mercenaries will know.
sentences.zh: 迦太基人非常擅长用刑，任何听过我们关于雇佣兵战争那一集的人都知道这一点。

sentences.en: And the men of the tribes that have been defeated will be enrolled into his own forces and they will be given incredibly lavish pay.
sentences.zh: 而被击败的部落士兵会被编入他自己的军队，并获得极其丰厚的薪水。

sentences.en: So this is the other side of the conquest that Hamilcar is very brutal to those who oppose him.
sentences.zh: 所以这是征服的另一面，哈米尔卡对反抗他的人极其残酷。

sentences.en: Those who back him, he will lavish all the gold that he's annexed and conquered.
sentences.zh: 对于支持他的人，他会慷慨地赏赐所有他吞并和征服得来的黄金。

sentences.en: And so this enables him to start spreading Carthaginian rule inland from the coaSt. And after about a decade of operations
sentences.zh: 这使得他能够开始将迦太基的统治从海岸向内陆蔓延。在西班牙进行了大约十年的军事行动后

sentences.en: in Spain, Hamilcar has a garrison there that's probably around 50,000 men.
sentences.zh: 哈米尔卡在那里拥有了一支大约五万人的守备部队。

sentences.en: So he's more than doubled it in the space of a decade.
sentences.zh: 所以他在十年内将兵力翻了一番还多。

sentences.en: And he's incredibly wealthy.
sentences.zh: 而且他富得流油。

sentences.en: His coffers are overflowing with silver.
sentences.zh: 他的国库里堆满了白银。

sentences.en: And unsurprisingly, the Romans are not really very thrilled about this.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，罗马人对此实在高兴不起来。

sentences.en: So by 231, they're sufficiently alarmed that they send an embassy to Hamilcar, basically saying, you know, hey, what's going on here?
sentences.zh: 因此到了公元前231年，他们感到足够惊慌，于是派出一个使团去见哈米尔卡，基本上是说，你知道的，嘿，这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: Hamilcar, his reply is, well, I'm raising funds to pay off the war indemnity that you illegally raised.
sentences.zh: 哈米尔卡的回答是，嗯，我正在筹集资金来偿还你们非法勒索的战争赔款。

sentences.en: And, you know, the Romans have to suck this up because I mean, it's a good reply.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，罗马人只能打碎牙齿往肚里咽，因为这个回答无懈可击。

sentences.en: And also, you know, as Hamilcar can point out, it's none of their business what he's getting up to in Spain.
sentences.zh: 而且，正如哈米尔卡所指出的，他在西班牙搞什么名堂根本不管罗马人屁事。

sentences.en: You know, this isn't covered by the treaty.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这不在条约的管辖范围内。

sentences.en: So the Roman ambassadors, you know, they're forced to bite their tongues and go back and accept the existence of this growing Carthaginian empire in Spain.
sentences.zh: 所以罗马大使们，你知道的，他们被迫打碎牙齿往肚里咽，回去接受西班牙日益壮大的迦太基帝国这一事实。

sentences.en: But then a bad blow for Hamilcar.
sentences.zh: 但接着对哈米尔卡来说是个沉重打击。

sentences.en: Well, a very bad blow, the worSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，极其沉重的打击，最糟的打击。

sentences.en: A exceedingly bad blow.
sentences.zh: 一个极其糟糕的打击。

sentences.en: He dies.
sentences.zh: 他死了。

sentences.en: In battle against whom?
sentences.zh: 在与谁的战斗中？

sentences.en: Against a Spanish tribe in the interior.
sentences.zh: 在与内陆一个西班牙部落的战斗中。

sentences.en: And the stories about how he dies become ever more extravagant as time goes by.
sentences.zh: 随着时间推移，关于他如何死去的传说变得越来越夸张。

sentences.en: So one historian is relatively close in time to the event and tends to be more sober.
sentences.zh: 所以有一位历史学家在时间上相对接近这一事件，往往更加清醒冷静。

sentences.en: He reports in very vague terms that Hamilcar ended his career in a manner which formed a fitting climax to his achievements, for he lost his life after fighting gallantly
sentences.zh: 他在记录中用非常模糊的词句提到，哈米尔卡的职业生涯以一种与其成就相配的高潮结束，因为他在英勇战斗后失去了生命

sentences.en: and with complete disregard for his personal safety in a battle against one of the strongest and most warlike of the tribes.
sentences.zh: 并且在与最强大、最好战的部落之一的战斗中完全置个人安危于不顾。

sentences.en: So it's a good death.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个壮烈的死法。

sentences.en: It's a heroic death.
sentences.zh: 这是一个英雄式的死法。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But accounts of exactly how he dies then start to get inflated.
sentences.zh: 但关于他究竟如何死去的说法随后开始被夸大。

sentences.en: So a later report says that he is betrayed by a local chieftain while undertaking a siege, that Hamilcar's forces are taken by surprise
sentences.zh: 因此，一份后来的报告称，他在进行围城战时遭到当地部落首领的背叛，哈米尔卡的军队遭到突袭

sentences.en: and they're forced to withdraw, that his two eldest sons, so that's Hannibal and Hamilcar, they are sent off by Hamilcar along one road and he then deliberately draws away the mass
sentences.zh: 并且被迫撤退，他的两个长子，也就是汉尼拔和哈米尔卡，被哈米尔卡派往一条道路，然后他通过走另一条路故意引开主力

sentences.en: of the enemy by taking another road.
sentences.zh: 大批的敌人。

sentences.en: He's about to be overtaken by his pursuers and ahead of him there's a raging river and he plunges into the river on his horse and drowns.
sentences.zh: 他快要被追兵追上了，前方是一条湍急的河流，他骑着马冲进河里淹死了。

sentences.en: So essentially he sacrifices himself for his two sons.
sentences.zh: 所以本质上他是为了两个儿子而牺牲了自己。

sentences.en: I mean, whether true or not, we don't know.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，不管是真是假，我们都不知道。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But he's like a kind of a lion defending his cubs.
sentences.zh: 但他就像是一头保护幼崽的雄狮。

sentences.en: I think that's dying rather than seeing his cubs exterminated.
sentences.zh: 我认为这宁可死去，也不愿看到自己的幼崽被消灭。

sentences.en: That's the theme.
sentences.zh: 这就是主题。

sentences.en: There's an element with him, isn't there, of the Philip of Macedon, Philip II.
sentences.zh: 他身上有一种马其顿的腓力，即腓力二世的影子，对吧？

sentences.en: For sure, yeah.
sentences.zh: 确实，是的。

sentences.en: So he ends up being famous as Hannibal's father.
sentences.zh: 所以他最终以汉尼拔的父亲的身份闻名。

sentences.en: But in both cases, you can argue the son's achievements are completely predicated on the successes of their father.
sentences.zh: 但在两种情况下，你可以说儿子的成就完全建立在他们父亲成功的基础之上。

sentences.en: So in both cases, their father leaves them with a lot of silver, a military machine, a load of officers they can
sentences.zh: 因此，在两种情况下，他们的父亲给他们留下了大量的白银、一台军事机器、一堆他们可以

sentences.en: rely on, a sense of prestige, you know, all the groundwork has been done basically.
sentences.zh: 依赖的军官、一种威望感，你知道的，基本上所有基础工作都做好了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And a kind of military education as well.
sentences.zh: 还有一种军事教育。

sentences.en: I mean, there is a difference though, that Hannibal, unlike Alexander, doesn't succeed his father immediately because he's still only 18.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，还是有区别的，汉尼拔不像亚历山大那样立即继承父亲的职位，因为他当时只有18岁。

sentences.en: He's not a king.
sentences.zh: 他不是国王。

sentences.en: You know, they don't have kings.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们没有国王。

sentences.en: So the leader of the Carthaginians in Spain is an elected post, essentially by the army, by the Carthaginians in the army.
sentences.zh: 所以西班牙迦太基人的领袖是一个选举产生的职位，基本上是由军队、由军队中的迦太基人选出来的。

sentences.en: And I think that people feel, well, an 18-year-old, he's too young.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为人们会觉得，嗯，一个18岁的年轻人，他太年轻了。

sentences.en: So they opt instead for Hasdrubal the Handsome, who is the young Hannibal's brother-in-law, Hasdrubal's son-in-law, very good-looking,
sentences.zh: 所以他们转而选择美男子哈斯德鲁巴，他是年轻汉尼拔的姐夫（或妹夫）、哈米尔卡的吉他手（此处原文为Son-in-law，译为哈米尔卡的女婿）、长相非常英俊，

sentences.en: King, Hamilcar's close political ally, has been with him in Spain, knows the ropes.
sentences.zh: 国王，哈米尔卡亲密的政治盟友，曾在西班牙与他共事，熟悉内情。

sentences.en: And Hamilcar, the handsome, is very effective.
sentences.zh: 而且美男子哈斯德鲁巴非常能干。

sentences.en: I mean, he's a worthy successor to Hamilcar.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他是哈米尔卡当之无愧的继任者。

sentences.en: And like Hamilcar had done, he kind of adopts this carrot and stick approach to the Iberians, to the peoples of Spain.
sentences.zh: 就像哈米尔卡过去所做的那样，他对伊比利亚人、对西班牙人民采取了一种胡萝卜加大棒的方法。

sentences.en: So he marries the daughter of an Iberian king.
sentences.zh: 所以他娶了一个伊比利亚国王的女儿。

sentences.en: So you asked about the dynastic quality.
sentences.zh: 所以你问到了王朝的特质。

sentences.en: I mean, there's a sense that this Carthaginian dynasty is starting to marry into local royalty.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，人们感觉到这个迦太基王朝开始与当地王室联姻。

sentences.en: He has himself proclaimed not just by the Carthaginians who have voted for him, but by the Iberians as general with unlimited power.
sentences.zh: 他不仅由投票支持他的迦太基人拥立，还被伊比利亚人拥立为拥有无限权力的统帅。

sentences.en: So he's rooting his authority in the colonized as well as the colonizers.
sentences.zh: 因此，他的统治基础既植根于被殖民者，也植根于殖民者。

sentences.en: And even as he's doing that, he's continuing this policy of absolutely brutal suppression of any hint of rebellion.
sentences.zh: 正当他这样做的时候，他仍在继续对任何叛乱迹象进行极其残酷镇压的政策。

sentences.en: And his first target, obviously, is the tribe that had killed Hamilcar.
sentences.zh: 他的第一个目标，显而易见，就是杀死哈米尔卡的那个部落。

sentences.en: They all get wiped out.
sentences.zh: 他们全都被消灭了。

sentences.en: So he is able to push Carthaginian control ever northwards towards the river Tagus, which is the great river that kind of flows through central Spain.
sentences.zh: 因此，他能够将迦太基的控制权进一步向北推进到特古斯河，这是一条流经西班牙中部的大河。

sentences.en: And this empire needs a new capital, Hasdrubal decides.
sentences.zh: 这个帝国需要一个新的首都，哈斯德鲁巴决定。

sentences.en: And so this is what he does.
sentences.zh: 这就是他所做的。

sentences.en: He founds a new capital and he calls it stunning originality, Carthage, which of course means new city.
sentences.zh: 他建立了一个新首都，并以惊人的原创力将其命名为“迦太基”，当然，这意为新城。

sentences.en: But the Romans in due course, we'll call it new Carthage, which effectively would be new, new city, but we'll call it new Carthage because otherwise it's very confusing.
sentences.zh: 但罗马人在适当时机，会称其为“新迦太基”，实际上这将是“新新城”，但我们还是叫它新迦太基，否则会非常混乱。

sentences.en: But the Carthaginians in Spain just called it Carthage.
sentences.zh: 但西班牙的迦太基人只管它叫迦太基。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And this is now in Spain?
sentences.zh: 这现在是在西班牙吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So it's Cartagena.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是卡塔赫纳。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Which to this day, I gather is still one of the kind of the main centers of the Spanish Navy.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，直到今天，它仍然是西班牙海军的主要中心之一。

sentences.en: So it's clearly, as the original Carthage is, a natural port, a great stronghold.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，就像最初的迦太基一样，它是一个天然的港口，一个伟大的要塞。

sentences.en: And it stands, there are kind of four hills dotted around this great natural harbor.
sentences.zh: 它矗立在那里，这个巨大的天然海港周围点缀着大约四座小山。

sentences.en: On the largest of these, Hasdrubal builds a great temple to the Carthaginian god of healing.
sentences.zh: 在其中最大的一座山上，哈斯德鲁巴为迦太基的医疗之神建造了一座宏伟的神庙。

sentences.en: And on the second largest, he builds his own vast palace, which is adorned with all the wealth of Spain.
sentences.zh: 在第二大的山丘上，他建造了自己的巨大宫殿，里面装饰着西班牙所有的财富。

sentences.en: And from there, he can sit and look down at the harbor and see growing numbers of ships, some of the military, but lots of the merchant ships swelling his coffers.
sentences.zh: 从那里，他可以坐下来俯瞰海港，看到越来越多的船只，有些是军舰，但有大量商船让他的金库充盈。

sentences.en: He's got the silver mines inland.
sentences.zh: 他拥有内陆的银矿。

sentences.en: He's got the shipping routes descending on his great capital.
sentences.zh: 他拥有通往他伟大首都的航运路线。

sentences.en: He's able to employ the most cutting edge military architects to build him walls around the city.
sentences.zh: 他能够聘请最尖端的军事建筑师为他修建城墙。

sentences.en: And so it's not surprising that it comes to be hailed by a near contemporary as the chief ornament and the center of the Carthaginian empire in Spain.
sentences.zh: 因此，它被一位近乎同时代的人誉为西班牙迦太基帝国的首席装饰和中心，也就不足为奇了。

sentences.en: So by the end of the 220s, the Carthaginians are back.
sentences.zh: 因此，到了公元前220年代末，迦太基人卷土重来。

sentences.en: I mean, they have an empire now.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们现在拥有一个帝国。

sentences.en: They have a land colony.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有一个陆地殖民地。

sentences.en: They have a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 他们有很多钱。

sentences.en: They have all the silver.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有所有的白银。

sentences.en: They have recruits.
sentences.zh: 他们有新兵。

sentences.en: They have rebuilt a lot of what they'd lost in the first Punic war against the Romans.
sentences.zh: 他们重建了在第一次对罗马布匿战争中失去的大部分东西。

sentences.en: Why therefore have very few listeners to this podcast heard of Hasdrubal?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么这个播客的极少数听众听说过哈斯德鲁巴呢？

sentences.en: What happened to him?
sentences.zh: 他怎么了？

sentences.en: In 221 BC, he gets assassinated by the slave of a disgruntled Iberian ally.
sentences.zh: 公元前221年，他被一个心怀不满的伊比利亚盟友的奴隶刺杀了。

sentences.en: Oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 哦，好吧。

sentences.en: And so, you know, that's the end of him.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，他的一生就这样结束了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But as you say, he has absolutely played his part in reconstituting Carthaginian power, possibly on a scale that is even greater than the power that Carthage had enjoyed before
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，他在重建迦太基力量方面绝对发挥了他的作用，其规模甚至可能大于迦太基在与罗马的

sentences.en: the first war with Rome.
sentences.zh: 第一次战争之前所享有的力量。

sentences.en: I mean, so absolutely, Carthage is back.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，毫无疑问，迦太基回来了。

sentences.en: She's a great power.
sentences.zh: 她是一个大国。

sentences.en: She can go eyeball to eyeball with Rome again.
sentences.zh: 她又能与罗马针锋相对了。

sentences.en: But there is obviously a slight paradox here, which is that all the power is now focused in Spain and Carthage herself back in Africa is slightly pallid in comparison.
sentences.zh: 但这里显然存在一点悖论，那就是现在所有的力量都集中在西班牙，相比之下，远在非洲本土的迦太基显得有些黯然失色。

sentences.en: It lacks the reserves.
sentences.zh: 它缺乏储备。

sentences.en: It lacks the wealth that is now starting to develop in new Carthage.
sentences.zh: 它缺乏现在开始在“新迦太基”发展起来的财富。

sentences.en: So that means that whoever is elected by the Carthaginian army to succeed Hasdrubal as the leader of Carthaginian power in Spain is probably in a position to
sentences.zh: 这意味着，无论谁被迦太基军队选举为哈斯德鲁巴的继任者，成为迦太基在西班牙势力的领袖，都可能处于一个能够

sentences.zh: 迦太基人，我觉得没打算这么做。

sentences.en: But indisputably, Hamilcar's ambition in raising his three sons for war is to restore Carthagin's status as great power.
sentences.zh: 但毫无疑问，哈米尔卡培养三个儿子去打仗的雄心，是为了恢复迦太基作为大国的地位。

sentences.en: And if this involves going to war with Rome, as Hamilcar clearly suspects it will, then so be it.
sentences.zh: 如果这意味着与罗马开战——正如哈米尔卡显然预料到的那样——那就开战吧。

sentences.en: You know, it will be the ultimate trial for his dynasty and for his city.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这将是对他的王朝和城市的终极考验。

sentences.en: And so Hannibal needs to be prepared for that trial.
sentences.zh: 所以汉尼拔需要为这场考验做好准备。

sentences.en: And it has to be said that Hamilcar, you know, prepares his eldest son for this great test unbelievably well.
sentences.zh: 必须指出的是，哈米尔卡为这场伟大的考验为其长子做准备的工作，做得好得令人难以置信。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And then when Hasdrubal, the handsome, succeeded Hamilcar, he had Hannibal as his cavalry commander, didn't he?
sentences.zh: 然后当“美男子”哈斯德鲁巴接替哈米尔卡时，他让汉尼拔担任他的骑兵指挥官，对吧？

sentences.en: There's no feuding there.
sentences.zh: 他们之间没有什么不和。

sentences.en: You might expect there to be tension between the two of them, but not at all.
sentences.zh: 你可能会觉得他们两人之间会有紧张关系，但一点也没有。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: And again, there's a comparison with Alexander, who as a young man commands Philip's cavalry.
sentences.zh: 同样，这也与亚历山大进行了对比，亚历山大年轻时曾指挥菲利普的骑兵。

sentences.en: By the time that Hannibal becomes supremo in Spain, he has established himself as a very formidable cavalry commander.
sentences.zh: 当汉尼拔成为西班牙的最高统帅时，他已经将自己确立为一名极其强大的骑兵指挥官。

sentences.en: But more than that, I think it's given him a sense of the importance and the potential of cavalry in expediting a sense of mobility.
sentences.zh: 但不仅如此，我认为这赋予了他对骑兵重要性和潜力的深刻理解，能以此带来更高的机动性。

sentences.en: And this, again, is something that he will display throughout his career.
sentences.zh: 这也是他在整个职业生涯中一直展现出来的特质。

sentences.en: And probably, you know, it's hard to think of a contemporary cavalry commander who could outclass Hannibal by the time he becomes kind of supremo in 221.
sentences.zh: 而且可能吧，很难想象在221年他成为最高统帅时，有哪个同时代的骑兵指挥官能胜过汉尼拔。

sentences.en: And this is, again, significant for Carthage's prospects in any land war with the Romans, because
sentences.zh: 这对迦太基在任何与罗马人的陆战中的前景都意义重大，因为

sentences.en: the Roman cavalry is definitely secondary to their infantry, which are heavy, heavily armoured and therefore potentially ponderous.
sentences.zh: 罗马骑兵绝对次于他们的步兵，罗马步兵是重步兵，全副武装，因此潜在行动较为迟缓。

sentences.en: So there is scope there.
sentences.zh: 所以这里有发挥的空间。

sentences.en: You know, there are things that Hannibal can make play with.
sentences.zh: 你知道，汉尼拔有很多可以施展身手的地方。

sentences.en: And again, just to reiterate this comparison with Alexander the Great, he's inherited this war machine.
sentences.zh: 再次重申与亚历山大大帝的对比，他继承了这台战争机器。

sentences.en: He's got this kind of early training as a cavalry commander.
sentences.zh: 他拥有这种早期的骑兵指挥官训练经历。

sentences.en: He's obviously personally very, very charismatic.
sentences.zh: 他显然个人极具个人魅力。

sentences.en: When he pointed out that Hasribal doesn't in any way seem to have been jealous of him, he clearly admires and respects Hannibal, even though he's younger and his obvious successor.
sentences.zh: 正如前面指出的，哈斯德鲁巴似乎并没有嫉妒过他，他显然很钦佩和尊重汉尼拔，尽管汉尼拔更年轻且显然是他的继承人。

sentences.en: He has all these young officers who've grown up around him, one of whom, Mago, his youngest brother, seems to have been particularly close to him.
sentences.zh: 他身边有一群围绕他长大的年轻军官，其中最小的弟弟马戈似乎与他格外亲近。

sentences.en: And he even has a Greek tutor who's a Spartan called Sosilus, who will accompany Hannibal on his campaigns and write up a biography.
sentences.zh: 他甚至还有一位希腊导师，是一个名叫索西卢斯的斯巴达人，他将陪同汉尼拔参加战役并撰写传记。

sentences.en: Again, that's very Alexander, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这又非常符合亚历山大的风格，对吧？

sentences.en: Having your own historian.
sentences.zh: 拥有属于自己的历史学家。

sentences.en: But do you think it's plausible that he was consciously modelling himself for Alexander, or is that overstated?
sentences.zh: 但你觉得他是有意识地模仿亚历山大，还是这种说法被夸大了？

sentences.en: Are we projecting that onto him with hindsight?
sentences.zh: 是我们事后诸葛亮地把这套强加给他的吗？

sentences.en: Well, Alexander's influence is manifested to the degree that Alexander is an influence on every general in the century that follows his great course of campaigns.
sentences.zh: 嗯，亚历山大的影响体现在：在他伟大的一系列战役之后的那个世纪里，亚历山大对每一位将军都有所影响。

sentences.en: But I don't think that Hannibal has anything like Alexander's desire to just push eastwards, ever eastwards.
sentences.zh: 但我认为汉尼拔根本没有亚历山大那种一心只想向东、不断向东推进的渴望。

sentences.en: Hannibal's goals are much more succinct, much more circumscribed.
sentences.zh: 汉尼拔的目标要精简得多，也更有局限性。

sentences.en: He essentially wants to re-establish Carthage as the greatest power in the Western Mediterranean.
sentences.zh: 他本质上是想恢复迦太基作为西地中海最强大国家的地位。

sentences.en: That will obviously require Rome to be humbled to a degree.
sentences.zh: 这显然需要让罗马在某种程度上屈服。

sentences.en: And so Hannibal is prepared to do that.
sentences.zh: 所以汉尼拔准备这么做。

sentences.en: But he doesn't, I think, want to obliterate Rome.
sentences.zh: 但我不认为他想彻底消灭罗马。

sentences.en: So if this means war with Rome, then Hannibal is prepared to go to war with Rome.
sentences.zh: 所以如果这意味着与罗马开战，那么汉尼拔已经做好了与罗马开战的准备。

sentences.en: But I think his preference would probably be, I'd rather not have war if we can possibly avoid it.
sentences.zh: 但我认为他的首选大概是：如果能尽量避免，我还是不想打仗。

sentences.en: He wants his empire in Spain.
sentences.zh: 他想要的是他在西班牙的帝国。

sentences.en: And if he can develop that empire in Spain without war with Rome, then all the better.
sentences.zh: 如果他能在不与罗马开战的情况下发展那个帝国，那就再好不过了。

sentences.en: But that's where the strong clouds of war begin together, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但战争的浓云正是在那里开始聚集的，不是吗？

sentences.en: In Spain.
sentences.zh: 在西班牙。

sentences.en: They do, yeah.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: The Romans by now have woken up to the fact that Spain is very lucrative.
sentences.zh: 罗马人此时已经意识到西班牙是一块非常肥沃的土地。

sentences.en: And Spain is going to be, as it were, the flashpoint, because they are not going to allow the Carthaginians just to occupy the entire peninsula.
sentences.zh: 西班牙即将成为一个导火索，因为他们不会允许迦太基人独占整个半岛。

sentences.en: Yeah, we say that.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们是这么说的。

sentences.en: But actually, the first treaty that establishes the relations between Carthage and Rome in Spain, it's brought about by a Roman position of weakness.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，确立迦太基与罗马在西班牙关系的第一个条约，其实是在罗马处于弱势的情况下促成的。

sentences.en: So in 225, the Romans are facing an invasion of Gauls.
sentences.zh: 所以在公元前225年，罗马人面临着高卢人的入侵。

sentences.en: So Gaul, what's now France?
sentences.zh: 高卢，也就是现在的法国？

sentences.en: And the Gauls had already, a century or so before, invaded Italy and actually captured Rome.
sentences.zh: 大约一个世纪前，高卢人就已经入侵过意大利并 실제로 攻占了罗马。

sentences.en: So the Romans are very, very anxious about Gauls.
sentences.zh: 因此罗马人对高卢人感到非常非常焦虑。

sentences.en: They know that they're a menacing enemy.
sentences.zh: 他们知道这是一个来势汹汹的敌人。

sentences.en: This invasion in 225 causes them great alarm.
sentences.zh: 公元前225年的这次入侵让他们深感恐慌。

sentences.en: And they're anxious that if the Gauls do invade Italy, then this will provide scope for the Carthaginians to start messing around.
sentences.zh: 他们担心如果高卢人真的入侵意大利，这会给迦太基人提供兴风作浪的空间。

sentences.en: So they sent an embassy to Hasribal, who's still alive at this point, and they sign a formal treaty.
sentences.zh: 于是他们派了一支使团去见当时还健在的哈斯德鲁巴，并签署了一份正式条约。

sentences.en: And by its terms, the Carthaginians pledge not to cross the river Ebro, which is a great river that joins the Mediterranean south of where Barcelona is today.
sentences.zh: 根据条约条款，迦太基人承诺不跨越埃布罗河，这是一条在巴塞罗那现址以南汇入地中海的大河。

sentences.en: And then it flows from the northwest in a line parallel to the Pyrenees.
sentences.zh: 它从西北发源，以平行于比利牛斯山的路线流淌。

sentences.en: And it's agreed that the Romans will accept everywhere south of the Ebro as being Carthaginian.
sentences.zh: 双方商定，罗马人承认埃布罗河以南的所有地方都属于迦太基。

sentences.en: And in the north, the Carthaginians will not kind of intrude north of the Ebro.
sentences.zh: 而在北部，迦太基人也不会在埃布罗河北岸进行某种程度的干涉。

sentences.en: But having signed this treaty, the Romans then can't help hedging their bets.
sentences.zh: 但签完这个条约后，罗马人却忍不住给自己留了后路。

sentences.en: And so shortly after they've signed this treaty with Hasribal, pledging that they won't poke their noses into Carthaginian affairs south of the river Ebro,
sentences.zh: 就在他们与哈斯德鲁巴签署条约、承诺不插手埃布罗河南岸的迦太基事务后不久，

sentences.en: they annihilate the Gallic invasion, which means that that threat is removed.
sentences.zh: 他们消灭了高卢人的入侵，这意味着这一威胁解除了。

sentences.en: And they start slightly regretting this treaty that they've signed.
sentences.zh: 他们开始对签署的这个条约感到有点后悔。

sentences.en: And so it's around the same time, and surely not coincidentally, that they establish friendly relations with an Iberian town called Saguntum, which lies on the coaSt.
sentences.zh: 差不多在同一时期，而且绝非巧合的是，他们与一个位于海岸边的伊比利亚城镇萨贡图姆建立了友好关系。

sentences.en: So very good communications with Rome by the sea.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们与罗马通过海路有着非常好的通讯联系。

sentences.en: And the Saguntines become the kind of the Romans' eyes in Spain, kind of sending the Romans' intelligence updates on what the Carthaginians are up to.
sentences.zh: 萨贡图姆人成了罗马人在西班牙的眼睛，向罗马人发送关于迦太基人动向的情报更新。

sentences.en: And they are qualified to do this because they lie just beyond the reach of Carthaginian control.
sentences.zh: 他们有资格这样做，因为他们刚好位于迦太基控制范围之外。

sentences.en: However, there is no guarantee that this will be permanently the case because Saguntum lies five miles south of the Ebro.
sentences.zh: 然而，这并不能保证永远如此，因为萨贡图姆位于埃布罗河以南五英里处。

sentences.en: Oh dear.
sentences.zh: 噢天哪。

sentences.en: Which means that according to the treaty that the Romans have signed with the Carthaginians, they are within the Carthaginian sphere of influence.
sentences.zh: 这意味着根据罗马人与迦太基人签署的条约，他们处于迦太基的影响范围之内。

sentences.en: I was about to say, when you look at a map, it's now Sagunto, which is not far from Valencia in the south of Spain.
sentences.zh: 我正想说，如果你看地图，它现在叫萨贡托，离西班牙南部的瓦伦西亚不远。

sentences.en: It clearly is a massive infringement of the treaty.
sentences.zh: 这显然是对条约的巨大践踏。

sentences.en: It absolutely is.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: And it's absolutely kind of classic.
sentences.zh: 而且这绝对可以说是非常经典的做法。

sentences.en: This is traditional Roman mischief making.
sentences.zh: 这就是罗马人传统的搞事作风。

sentences.en: There is massive scope for a bust up.
sentences.zh: 这里有巨大的冲突空间。

sentences.en: However, the crisis does take time to brew because to begin with,
sentences.zh: 不过，危机的酝酿确实需要时间，因为一开始，

sentences.en: Hannibal's focus is not on Saguntum.
sentences.zh: 汉尼拔的焦点不在萨贡图姆。

sentences.en: What he wants to do is secure Carthaginian control deep into central Spain, along the line of the River Tagus, this river that flows through the center of the peninsula.
sentences.zh: 他想做的是沿着塔古斯河——这条流经半岛中心的河流——将迦太基的控制力巩固到西班牙中部腹地。

sentences.en: And he's essentially following Hasdrubal the Handsome's policy.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是在遵循“美男子”哈斯德鲁巴的政策。

sentences.en: So he too takes a Spanish wife.
sentences.zh: 所以他也娶了一位西班牙妻子。

sentences.en: He wants to make sure of the loyalty of the Iberians as well as of the Carthaginians.
sentences.zh: 他希望确保伊比利亚人以及迦太基人的忠诚。

sentences.en: Again, he's very happy to take the fight to those Iberians who oppose him.
sentences.zh: 同样，他非常乐于跟那些反对他的伊比利亚人开战。

sentences.en: He fights two brilliant campaigns in 2.22, 2.21.
sentences.zh: 在公元前222年和221年，他打出了两场精彩的战役。

sentences.en: He wins his first major pitched battle.
sentences.zh: 他赢得了他的第一场重大野战。

sentences.en: It's against enemies who massively outnumber him.
sentences.zh: 对手的数量远超于他。

sentences.en: He wipes them out by drawing them in.
sentences.zh: 他通过引诱将他们全歼。

sentences.en: He tricks them, divides them up, surrounds them, wipes them out with elephants.
sentences.zh: 他智取他们、将其分割、包围，并用大象将他们消灭。

sentences.en: So again, there's lots of kind of pointers there to the kind of military courses he'll be adopting.
sentences.zh: 所以，这里面再次有很多迹象表明他将采用的军事路线。

sentences.en: He storms towns.
sentences.zh: 他攻城拔寨。

sentences.en: He takes loot.
sentences.zh: 他夺取战利品。

sentences.en: He rewards his troops very, very lavishly.
sentences.zh: 他非常非常大方地奖赏他的军队。

sentences.en: And it becomes apparent that his men really adore him because he gives them victory.
sentences.zh: 显而易见，他的手下真的非常崇拜他，因为他给他们带来了胜利。

sentences.en: He makes them rich.
sentences.zh: 他让他们变得富有。

sentences.en: And it's evident that he cares for them kind of very, very deeply.
sentences.zh: 并且很明显，他非常非常深切地关爱着他们。

sentences.en: So the more campaigns Hannibal conducts, the more he can be confident that his war machine is really primed and ready to go.
sentences.zh: 因此，汉尼拔进行的战役越多，他就越能确信自己的战争机器已经真正蓄势待发。

sentences.en: And now that he's got almost the whole of central Spain conquered, his eye turns to the last stretch south of the Ebro by which, according to a treaty with Rome,
sentences.zh: 现在他几乎征服了整个西班牙中部，他的目光转向了埃布罗河以南的最后一段，根据与罗马的条约，

sentences.en: he's entitled to conquer.
sentences.zh: 他有权征服这里。

sentences.en: And that's the coastal stretch, which, of course, includes Saguntum.
sentences.zh: 这就是沿海地带，当然，其中就包括萨贡图姆。

sentences.en: And so in the year 220, at the end of the campaigning season, he returns to New Carthage.
sentences.zh: 于是在公元前220年，在作战季节结束时，他回到了新迦太基。

sentences.en: Everybody knows that Saguntum is ready for the following year and he finds a Roman embassy waiting for him.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道萨贡图姆在为来年做准备，而他发现一个罗马使团正在那里等他。

sentences.en: And so do they give him, what, a settlement, an ultimatum?
sentences.zh: 那么他们是给了他一份协议，还是最后通牒？

sentences.en: What have they got in their locker?
sentences.zh: 他们的底牌是什么？

sentences.en: They issue him a formal caution and, to quote Livy, that he should leave the people of Saguntum in peace as allies of the Roman people.
sentences.zh: 他们向他发出了正式警告，用李维的话来说，就是他应该让萨贡图姆人民作为罗马人民的盟友安居乐业。

sentences.en: And Hannibal treats this with absolute scorn.
sentences.zh: 而汉尼拔对此报以绝对的蔑视。

sentences.en: I mean, he clearly finds the tone of the ambassadors very offensive.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他显然觉得大使们的语气极具挑衅性。

sentences.en: You know, Carthage and Rome have this treaty.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，迦太基和罗马有这个条约。

sentences.en: He can do what he likes to Saguntum by the terms of that treaty.
sentences.zh: 根据条约条款，他对萨贡图姆想做什么都可以。

sentences.en: And I think more than that, it would have reminded him of how the Romans had played this trick before, because essentially the war in Sicily that kicked off the first Punic war,
sentences.zh: 我认为不仅如此，这会让他想起罗马人以前是怎么玩这种把手的，因为引发第一次布匿战争的西西里战争本质上也是如此，

sentences.en: so the first great conflict between Rome and Carthage, the Romans had pulled exactly the same stunt.
sentences.zh: 也就是罗马和迦太基之间的第一次大战冲突，罗马人当时就玩了完全相同的把戏。

sentences.en: They had invaded Sicily with the defense that they were defending friends that they'd recruited in Sicily.
sentences.zh: 他们入侵西西里的借口是他们在保卫自己在西西里结交的朋友。

sentences.en: And that had obviously ended up with the Romans conquering the whole island.
sentences.zh: 这显然最终导致罗马人征服了整个岛屿。

sentences.en: And Hannibal knows the Romans have form here.
sentences.zh: 汉尼拔知道罗马人在这一套上是有前科的。

sentences.en: He's determined not to allow the Romans to get a foothold in Spain and to try and play the same trick there.
sentences.zh: 他决不允许罗马人在西班牙立足，并在那里故伎重施。

sentences.en: So he plays the Romans at their own game.
sentences.zh: 所以他以其人之道还治其人之身。

sentences.en: And he says that he has friends in Saguntum and they're being menaced by our style faction by the Romans.
sentences.zh: 他说他在萨贡图姆有朋友，他们正受到罗马人支持的一派人的威胁。

sentences.en: So basically it's his moral duty to attack and capture Saguntum.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上他的道义职责就是进攻并攻占萨贡图姆。

sentences.en: I mean, he's clearly studied Roman diplomacy as well as military techniques very closely.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他显然对罗马的外交以及军事手段进行过非常深入的研究。

sentences.en: And he's doing exactly what the Romans do.
sentences.zh: 他正在做罗马人常做的事。

sentences.en: So we're in 220.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在在公元前220年。

sentences.en: So you can see very clearly how in 219, 280, 270, this might lead to war, right?
sentences.zh: 所以你可以非常清楚地看到，在公元前219年、280年、270年，这怎么就会导致战争，对吧？

sentences.en: There's this flashpoint and the irreconcilable positions.
sentences.zh: 存在这个导火索和不可调和的立场。

sentences.en: Yeah, because I think it's clear that in 219, Hannibal is absolutely set on attacking Saguntum.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为我认为很显然，在公元前219年，汉尼拔是铁了心要进攻萨贡图姆的。

sentences.en: But he didn't have to, right?
sentences.zh: 但他本不必如此，对吧？

sentences.en: So there were, even at the time, there were ancient historians, ancient authors who thought he could have made a different choice.
sentences.zh: 所以即使在当时，也有古代历史学家和古代作家认为他本可以做出不同的选择。

sentences.en: And then history would have unfolded completely differently.
sentences.zh: 那么历史就会完全朝着另一个方向发展。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So it was said in the wake of the war, Hannibal's war, that he could have asked the Romans to hand back Sardinia, for instance,
sentences.zh: 所以在战争结束后，据说汉尼拔本可以要求罗马人归还萨丁尼亚，例如，

sentences.en: and to remit the indemnity that had been illegally imposed on them.
sentences.zh: 并免除强加给他们的非法赔偿金。

sentences.en: Were they ever going to do that?
sentences.zh: 他们会答应这种事吗？

sentences.en: That seems so un-Roman.
sentences.zh: 这太不符合罗马人的作风了。

sentences.en: It seems so unlikely that they would ever have done that.
sentences.zh: 他们绝无可能这么做，这看起来太不可能了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: That's obviously why Hannibal never even thought to adopt that policy, because it was never going to happen.
sentences.zh: 这显然就是为什么汉尼拔甚至从未想过采取那种政策，因为这根本不可能发生。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: The Romans would never have agreed to surrender Sardinia, because that's not what the Romans do.
sentences.zh: 罗马人绝不会同意交出萨丁尼亚，因为这不是罗马人的行事风格。

sentences.en: And anyway, Hannibal is probably thinking, no, suppose I do attack in an exaguntum.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，汉尼拔可能在想，不，假设我真的进攻萨贡图姆。

sentences.en: You know, what are the Romans going to do about it?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，罗马人能把我怎么样？

sentences.en: Rome is a long way from Spain.
sentences.zh: 罗马离西班牙很远。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Are they really going to risk war over this one city?
sentences.zh: 他们真的会为了这一个城市而冒开战的风险吗？

sentences.en: And even if they do, bring it on.
sentences.zh: 即使他们真的要打，那就放马过来吧。

sentences.en: You know, I've got this amazing army.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我有这支无敌的军队。

sentences.en: I'm ready to go.
sentences.zh: 我已经准备好出发了。

sentences.en: It's clear that Hannibal is not alone in thinking this.
sentences.zh: 很显然，这么想的不止汉尼拔一个人。

sentences.en: The Senate back in Carthage think this too, because the Roman embassy that had been to see Hannibal then go to Carthage to complain about Hannibal's behavior.
sentences.zh: 远在迦太基的元老院也是这么想的，因为去见汉尼拔的罗马使团随后去了迦太基，抱怨汉尼拔的行为。

sentences.en: And the Senate there, even though lots of them don't particularly like Hannibal and are kind of jealous of him, they basically say, you know, piss off.
sentences.zh: 那里的元老院尽管很多人其实并不喜欢汉尼拔，而且对他有点嫉妒，但他们基本上还是说，滚一边去吧。

sentences.en: We're not having this, you know.
sentences.zh: 我们可不吃这一套。

sentences.en: So essentially there is a Carthaginian united front.
sentences.zh: 所以本质上，迦太基形成了一个统一战线。

sentences.en: And this means that in the early summer of 219, Hannibal embarks on the siege of Saguntum, knowing that he has the full backing of everyone in his native city.
sentences.zh: 这意味着在公元前219年夏初，汉尼拔在深知得到祖国所有人全力支持的情况下，开始了对萨贡图姆的围攻。

sentences.en: And yet at first, I mean, you've been talking up Hannibal and his war machine, but at first that siege of Saguntum doesn't go terribly well for him.
sentences.zh: 然而一开始，我的意思是，你之前一直在吹捧汉尼拔和他的战争机器，但一开始对萨贡图姆的围攻对他来说并不太顺利。

sentences.en: No, it's a disaster, actually.
sentences.zh: 不，实际上是一场灾难。

sentences.en: He gets wounded in the thigh, which isn't very helpful.
sentences.zh: 他的大腿受了伤，这可真不是什么好事。

sentences.en: And I think in general, Hannibal is better in the field than he is kind of laying siege to cities.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为总的来说，汉尼拔在野战中的表现要好过他围攻城市。

sentences.en: So all through the summer, all through the autumn, into the winter, Saguntum still hasn't fallen.
sentences.zh: 所以在整个夏天、整个秋天，一直到冬天，萨贡图姆仍然没有陷落。

sentences.en: And had the Romans intervened, then it could potentially have been a real problem for Hannibal.
sentences.zh: 如果罗马人当时进行了干预，那么这对外围的汉尼拔来说可能真的会成为一个大问题。

sentences.en: But the Romans don't intervene.
sentences.zh: 但罗马人没有干预。

sentences.en: And the reason for that is essentially, it's a bit like Britain in the 30s.
sentences.zh: 原因本质上是，这有点像三十年代的英国。

sentences.en: You know, there's massive disagreement.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，存在着巨大的分歧。

sentences.en: There's a kind of war party and they're saying, you know, we've got to do this or else, you know, it's going to lead to disaster.
sentences.zh: 有一派主战派说，你知道的，我们必须这么做，否则就会酿成大祸。

sentences.en: And there are others who say, oh, I'm not sure about that.
sentences.zh: 还有另一派说，哦，这我可说不准。

sentences.en: And so these disagreements in Rome enable Hannibal to prosecute the siege until in early 218, the city finally falls.
sentences.zh: 因此，罗马内部的这些分歧让汉尼拔得以继续围城，直到公元前218年初，这座城市终于陷落。

sentences.en: The city is stripped of all its treasure.
sentences.zh: 这座城市被掠夺一空。

sentences.en: The population are either slaughtered or sold into slavery.
sentences.zh: 人口要么被屠杀，要么被卖为奴隶。

sentences.en: It's an absolute triumph for Hannibal.
sentences.zh: 这对汉尼拔来说是一场绝对的胜利。

sentences.en: And back in Rome, the news of this prompts intense feelings of anger, but also, I think, of shame.
sentences.zh: 在罗马，听到这个消息引发了强烈的愤怒，但我也认为，还有羞耻感。

sentences.en: And from this point on, the Romans will never cease to characterize the capture of Saguntum as a terrible war crime of the kind that they themselves would never commit.
sentences.zh: 从这一刻起，罗马人将不断把攻占萨贡图姆定性为一种可怕的战争罪行，这是他们自己绝不会犯下的那种罪行。

sentences.en: But, I mean, this, it seems like such a standard thing, but also the kind of thing the Romans did all the time.
sentences.zh: 但是，我的意思是，这看起来像是标准操作，但也正是罗马人一直在做的那种事。

sentences.en: Absolutely is.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: So the hypocrisy of the Romans in this, I think, is quite something.
sentences.zh: 所以罗马人在这件事上的虚伪，我认为相当惊人。

sentences.en: And I think that there are still elements within the Roman Senate who recognize this.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为罗马元老院内部仍然有人意识到了这一点。

sentences.en: So there is a still, it's not exactly a peace party, but it's a faction that says, oh, are we really sure we want to go to war over this?
sentences.zh: 所以仍然存在着一个——虽然算不上是和平派，但算是一个派别——他们说，哦，我们真的确信我们要为此开战吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And this faction is led by a very distinguished senatorial figure called Quintus Fabius Maximus Verucusus.
sentences.zh: 这个派别由一位非常杰出的参议员领导，名叫昆图斯·法比乌斯·马克西姆·韦鲁库苏斯。
zh_words: 昆图斯·法比乌斯·马克西姆·韦鲁库苏斯

sentences.en: So warty, a bit like Oliver Cromwell.
sentences.zh: 所以是个有疣的人，有点像奥利弗·克伦威尔。

sentences.en: He's got a wart on his nose.
sentences.zh: 他的鼻子上有个疣。

sentences.en: And he says, look, before we declare war, let's put out the peace feelers again.
sentences.zh: 他说，听着，在我们宣战之前，让我们再次试探一下和平的可能。

sentences.en: Let's send an embassy to Carthage.
sentences.zh: 让我们向迦太基派遣使团。

sentences.en: You know, let's see if we can open feelers to Hannibal's enemies in Carthage and just try and avoid open war.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，看看我们能否向汉尼拔在迦太基的敌人们抛出橄榄枝，并尽量避免全面战争。

sentences.en: And I think this is partly because, you know, they think the war might be quite difficult,
sentences.zh: 我认为这部分是因为，你知道的，他们觉得这场战争可能会相当艰难，

sentences.en: but also because genuinely the Romans are a very kind of moralistic people and they don't want the guilt of starting the war.
sentences.zh: 但也是因为罗马人确实是一个非常有道德感的民族，他们不想背负挑起战争的罪名。

sentences.en: They're trying to absolutely pin the blame for any conflict on the Carthaginians.
sentences.zh: 他们正试图把任何冲突的责任完全归咎于迦太基人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: So the Roman embassy goes to Carthage and they arrive there.
sentences.zh: 于是罗马使团前往迦太基并抵达了那里。

sentences.en: But despite this kind of, you know, let's go negotiate with the Carthaginians, they're Romans.
sentences.zh: 但尽管有着这种“让我们去和迦太基人谈判”的姿态，他们毕竟是罗马人。

sentences.en: They're not really there to negotiate.
sentences.zh: 他们并不是真的为了谈判而去的。

sentences.en: And their starting demand is so obviously impossible that effectively they're wasting their breath.
sentences.zh: 他们开出的初始要求如此明显地不可能实现，以至于他们实际上是在白费口舌。

sentences.en: And their starting demand is that Hannibal should be surrendered to the Romans.
sentences.zh: 他们提出的初始要求是必须将汉尼拔交予罗马人。

sentences.en: And there's no way that the Carthaginians are going to do this.
sentences.zh: 迦太基人绝不可能这么做。

sentences.en: Even Hannibal's bitterest enemies can recognize that if they hand over the guy who's in charge of Carthaginian Spain, that will be the end of Spain.
sentences.zh: 即使是汉尼拔最死硬的政敌也清楚，如果他们交出这位掌管迦太基西班牙事务的负责人，西班牙就彻底完了。

sentences.en: You know, the Romans will move in.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，罗马人会大举进驻。

sentences.en: No question.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问。

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 对，当然。

sentences.en: And so negotiations go nowhere.
sentences.zh: 于是谈判陷入了僵局。

sentences.en: And the leading Roman ambassador, who may be Quintus Fabius Maximus or perhaps his cousin, the sources are contradictory.
sentences.zh: 罗马首席大使，可能是昆图斯·法比乌斯·马克西姆斯，也可能是他的表弟，史料对此莫衷一是。
zh_words: 昆图斯·法比乌斯·马克西姆斯

sentences.en: He stands up, a very famous scene, and I'll quote a Roman source that describes it.
sentences.zh: 他站起身来，这是一个非常著名的场景，我将引用一个罗马史料来描述它。

sentences.en: He pointed to the bosom of his toga and declared to the Carthaginian Senate that in its folds he carried both peace and war and that he would let fall from it whichever they instructed him to leave.
sentences.zh: 他指着自己的托加长袍胸前，向迦太基元老院宣称，他的衣褶里既装有和平也装有战争，他们让他留下哪个，他就从里面掉落哪个。

sentences.en: The Carthaginian chief magistrate answered that he should bring out whichever he thought beSt.
sentences.zh: 迦太基最高长官回答说，他应该拿出他认为最好的一样。

sentences.en: And when the envoy replied that it would be war, many of the senators, so those are the Carthaginians, shouted at once, we accept it.
sentences.zh: 当使者回答说是战争时，许多元老——也就是那些迦太基人——立刻大声喊道，我们接受。

sentences.en: It was on these terms that the Senate and the Roman ambassadors parted.
sentences.zh: 就在这样的条件下，元老院和罗马使者分道扬镳了。

sentences.en: So, the storm clouds of war have not merely gathered, Tom.
sentences.zh: 所以，汤姆，战争的阴云不仅聚拢了。

sentences.en: The storm is underway.
sentences.zh: 风暴已经爆发了。

sentences.en: Yeah, as Chris Morris would say, it's war.
sentences.zh: 是的，正如克里斯·莫里斯所说，这就是战争。

sentences.en: It is war.
sentences.zh: 这就是战争。

sentences.en: And there's so much to come in this story.
sentences.zh: 这个故事里还有太多的内容要讲。

sentences.en: There's elephants.
sentences.zh: 有大象。

sentences.en: There's crossing the Alps.
sentences.zh: 有翻越阿尔卑斯山。

sentences.en: There's tremendous battles.
sentences.zh: 有激烈的战役。

sentences.en: The Battle of Trebia, the Battle of Lake Trasimene.
sentences.zh: 特雷比亚战役，特拉西门湖战役。

sentences.en: And finally, at the end of this mighty series, one of the great battles in all ancient history, indeed in history, full stop, the Battle of Cannae.
sentences.zh: 最后，在这个宏大系列的末尾，是古代历史上所有战役中最伟大的战役之一，甚至可以说是整个历史上最伟大的战役——坎尼战役。

sentences.en: Anyway, so, Tom, what can people do if they want to hear all this story right away?
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，汤姆，如果大家想立刻听到所有这些故事，该怎么做呢？

sentences.en: Well, Dominic, in a stunning innovation, we've set up a private club which enables you to access all four episodes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，多米尼克，在一项令人惊叹的创新中，我们建立了一个私人俱乐部，让你能够收听所有四集节目。

sentences.en: And it's very simple.
sentences.zh: 而且非常简单。

sentences.en: You go to therestishistory.com and very, very reasonably priced, isn't it, Dominic?
sentences.zh: 你访问 therestishistory.com，价格非常非常公道，对吧，多米尼克？

sentences.en: Very reasonably priced.
sentences.zh: 价格非常公道。

sentences.en: Basically giving it away.
sentences.zh: 基本上跟白送一样。

sentences.en: Yeah, basically.
sentences.zh: 对，基本上是的。

sentences.en: So, that's what you can do.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是你可以做的。

sentences.en: And you can get all four episodes there.
sentences.zh: 你可以在那里收听所有四集。

sentences.en: And listen, these episodes will be some of the most epic, the most swashbuckling, the most bloody, and the most glamorous that we've ever done in the rest of this history.
sentences.zh: 听着，这些节目将是我们《历史其余部分》节目中做过的最具史诗感、最惊险刺激、最血腥、也最迷人的节目之一。

sentences.en: Do not miss it.
sentences.zh: 千万不要错过。

sentences.en: Tom, thank you so much for that.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，非常感谢你分享这些。

sentences.zh: 我们下期再见。
